title: Why Sinks Gurgle: Siphonage and Venting
description: Siphonage occurs when flowing water fills a drain pipe, creating a negative pressure zone behind it. If the fixture lacks proper atmospheric venting or if the vent stack is clogged with debris, the vacuum pulls water out of the trap seal. A compromised P-trap seal allows sewer gas to escape into the living space. Troubleshooting requires inspecting the roof vent terminal for bird nests, leaves, or frost closure, and verifying air admittance valves or vent branch functionality using camera inspection.

Why Sinks Gurgle: Siphonage and Venting

Siphonage occurs when flowing water fills a drain pipe, creating a negative pressure zone behind it. If the fixture lacks proper atmospheric venting or if the vent stack is clogged with debris, the vacuum pulls water out of the trap seal. A compromised P-trap seal allows sewer gas to escape into the living space. Troubleshooting requires inspecting the roof vent terminal for bird nests, leaves, or frost closure, and verifying air admittance valves or vent branch functionality using camera inspection.
